_comment: The `build` field's resolution order and its accepted revision vocabulary.
docs/CONTRACTS.md prose says the same thing; this is the machine-readable
half, so a change to the order or the vocabulary moves a fixture instead of
Added 2026-09-07 with the npm package. `npm` is new: before it, an installed
copy fell through to `unknown`, because there is no repository to ask. That
made the field worthless in the one place provenance is hardest to
reconstruct afterwards -- an installed binary cannot know its commit, but
'this is a published build' is true, checkable, and more than nothing.
Order is significant: the first rule that produces a value wins.

resolution_order.when: the environment variable is set and non-blank
resolution_order.note: the only form that carries a real commit through npm install; release archives ship it in a GNOMON_BUILD file

resolution_order.when: git answers rev-parse in the harness's own source directory
resolution_order.revision: <short sha>, suffixed -dirty when the worktree has uncommitted changes

resolution_order.when: git does not answer and the harness is running from inside a node_modules tree

must_never: end with a bare '+' — a missing revision is said, never implied
claim a commit for a tree with uncommitted changes
